chunks: Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bakr al-Bakr al-Khazz in Naysaboor narrated that Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Khwar said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad the Jurist al-Khwar narrated that Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Joybari al-Shaybani, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, destined the destinies and arranged the plans two thousand years before the creation of Adam.
ai.seo_question: When did God decree the destinies according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali al-Ridha (peace be upon him), recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, emphasizes the pre-eternal nature of divine decree (al-maqadir) and planning (al-tadabir) prior to the creation of Adam. It underscores the Shia theological understanding that God’s knowledge and will encompass all events before their temporal manifestation, linking the concept of *al-maqadir* to the broader framework of divine omniscience and predestination.
